exposure: Exteriorization of the uterus during Cesarean section (CS)
In situ repair of the uterus during Cesarean section (CS)
cohort: 200 patients undergoing Cesarean section were randomized into two groups: exteriorization (n=100) and in situ repair (n=100).
finding: Exteriorization of the uterus during CS significantly reduced surgery time and blood loss but was associated with higher immediate postoperative pain compared to in situ repair.
mod_finding: Exteriorization of the uterus during Cesarean section leads to reduced surgery time and blood loss but increased immediate postoperative pain, with similar maternal and neonatal outcomes, except for a slightly higher 5-minute APGAR score in the in situ group.
followup_time: 5 minutes post-birth (for neonatal outcomes); up to hospital discharge (for maternal outcomes)
